### Overview

<section class="icon-stats">

::: {.icon-card}
<img src="../assets/icons/calendar.svg" alt="Founded">
<h4>Founded in 1954</h4>
<p>
  Carries out activities of documentation, identification and preservation of plants, supporting teaching, scientific research and biodiversity conservation.
</p>
:::

::: {.icon-card}
<img src="../assets/icons/plant.svg" alt="Herbarium">
<h4> 300,000+ records</h4>
<p>
  The largest herbarium in the Brazilian Amazon and the 5th largest in Brazil. Brazilian flora accounts for more than 90% of the specimens, making it a national and international reference.
</p>
:::

::: {.icon-card}
<img src="../assets/icons/fungi.svg" alt="Fungi">
<h4> 30,000+ records</h4>
<p>
 An important reference for fungi of the Amazon region, especially macrofungi.
</p>
:::

::: {.icon-card}
<img src="../assets/icons/briofitas.svg" alt="Bryophytes">
<h4> 20,000+ records</h4>
<p>A collection of Amazonian mosses and liverworts, important for understanding the biodiversity and conservation of these groups.</p>
:::

::: {.icon-card}
<img src="../assets/icons/wood.svg" alt="Xylarium">
<h4> 10,000+ records</h4>
<p>
  The xylarium (wood collection) has great scientific, historical and cultural value, and is a reference for studies of the region's biodiversity.
</p>
:::

::: {.icon-card}
<img src="../assets/icons/carpo.svg" alt="Carpological collection">
<h4> 3,000+ records</h4>
<p>
 The most representative carpological (fruit and seed) collection in the Amazon. It contributes significantly to the systematics of Amazonian fruits.
</p>
:::

::: {.cta-section}
### Visit the collection

<p class="text-justify">
The INPA Herbarium collection is currently available on the
<strong><i>species</i>Link</strong> network platform, which brings together
biological records from several regions of Brazil and South America.
</p>

::: cta-wrapper
<a class="cta-button"
     href="https://specieslink.net/search/records/col/694"
     target="_blank"> Access the virtual collection \> </a>
:::
:::
